tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: List the Google accounts signed in to the saved session with their /u/<N>/ slot. Call first and confirm with the user which email holds their photos.

tools.name: list_media
tools.description: Page through the Google Photos library timeline, newest first: media key, taken/uploaded time, dimensions, photo or video (+duration), favorite flag and a thumbnail URL. Optional date range (after/before) and type filter. Pass next_page_token to continue.

tools.name: search_media
tools.description: Search the library the way the Google Photos search box does: free text (sunset, food, beach), a person's name from People, a place, or a thing. Returns the same item shape as list_media.

tools.name: get_media
tools.description: Full metadata for one item: filename, taken time and timezone offset, file size, dimensions, photo/video and duration, camera make/model/aperture/ISO/exposure when present, face count and named people, favorite flag, location (latitude/longitude from the file's GPS plus Google's place name; null whe

tools.name: download_media
tools.description: Save the bytes of a thumbnail at any size or the original file to a local folder and return the path (plus sha256, and base64 for small files when asked). The image URLs need the signed-in cookies, so always fetch through this tool.

tools.name: list_albums
tools.description: List the user's albums (album_key, title, created), or pass album_key to list the items inside that album.

tools.name: create_album
tools.description: Create a new album with a title, optionally adding library items to it straight away.

tools.name: add_to_album
tools.description: Add library items to an existing album.

tools.name: remove_from_album
tools.description: Remove items from an album. The photos stay in the library; only the album membership changes.

tools.name: set_favorite
tools.description: Mark items as favorites (favorite=true, default) or remove the favorite (favorite=false).

tools.name: archive_media
tools.description: Archive items (they leave the main photo grid but stay in albums, search and Archive), or unarchive with archive=false.

tools.name: trash_media
tools.description: Move items to Google Photos' Trash, where they stay recoverable for 60 days. Never deletes permanently and cannot empty the Trash. Requires confirm=true; max 50 items per call. Show the user the exact items and get their yes first.

tools.name: upload_media
tools.description: Upload a local photo or video file (up to 10 GB) into the library, optionally into an album. Sent in resumable chunks, so a dropped connection resumes instead of restarting. Returns the new item. Uploading a file that is already in the library returns the existing item.

tools.name: check_session
tools.description: Check that the saved Google Photos session still works and list the signed-in accounts. Read-only: it never refreshes the session. If it reports the session expired, the user reconnects with start_browser_auth.

tools.name: start_browser_auth
tools.description: Open Google Photos sign-in only when needed. If the saved session is still valid, this tool returns success immediately and does not open the viewer. Call session_status first. Use force_reconnect only when the user explicitly wants to wipe the saved cookie and sign in again (destructive).

tools.name: get_network_identity
tools.description: Where this user's requests to the site leave from (a VPN country, the server, or the app's default) and which browser they present. Read-only.

tools.name: set_network_identity
tools.description: Choose where this user's requests to the site leave from and which browser they present, only when the user asks (e.g. 'connect through Nigeria', 'use my own user agent'). Sites may ask the user to sign in again when this changes. reset=true goes back to how they signed in.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "download_media" references sensitive artifacts (cookie). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp-google_photos" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_accounts, list_media, get_media, download_media · Private data: get_media, download_media, upload_media · Public sink: list_accounts, upload_media · Destructive: remove_from_album, set_favorite, set_network_identity.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_accounts, list_media, get_media, download_media · Private data: get_media, download_media, upload_media · Public sink: list_accounts, upload_media · Destructive: remove_from_album, set_favorite, set_network_identity

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
